timing: One single-thread CPU process per puzzle; wall-clock budget includes initial ordinary GAC, proposal adapter/context setup, generation/decoding, planning, contraction and GAC. Model/network/state loading, source hashing, final validation, disk publication and residual DFS are excluded. Closed-domain snapshots are copied in RAM inside the timed interval. Completion timestamps are sampled after full contraction+GAC and lightweight accounting, before snapshot copying. Both wall and CPU timestamps are recorded. SIGALRM interrupts read-only proposals/planning; blocked during initial GAC and domain mutation/contraction+GAC. Atomic completion after a budget earns no earlier credit.
interpretation: Exploratory replication on all 100 previously evaluated puzzles, without performance-based selection. All nine methods rerun from the original domains, on the same worker per puzzle, with fixed checkpoints, decoders and per-cluster limits. One 300s trajectory supplies prefixes 1/5/15/60/120/300s; no saved trajectory is resumed or spliced into this replication. The generic mix shares one aggregate budget across heuristic/teacher/REINFORCE/replay/Q, restarting their iterators after useful pruning on shared updated domains. It targets equal cumulative wall shares with nonpreemptive one-candidate turns, not hard per-source quotas. Switching, proposal, planning, contraction and GAC are charged; no Sudoku expert or untrained control enters the mix. The expert remains a separate reference with its original larger limits. Model/network/state loading is excluded. Hardware is recorded per attempt; do not merge these timings with old runs.
scheduling: least cumulative charged source wall time; one candidate turn
execution: One one-thread CPU job per puzzle; all nine methods sequentially on the same worker, in seeded random order. Respect scheduler affinity. A restarted job reruns the whole puzzle in a separate attempt; only a complete attempt publishes a completion marker. Residual plain MAC is separate.
